title: Basemap layer set
description: Declares the raster basemap layers a module offers behind its map view, in the terrain / street / satellite idiom users expect from Google, Bing and Apple Maps. Deliberately provider-agnostic: a viewer implements the tile protocol, never a specific vendor's SDK. Credentials are NEVER stored in this document. See BASEMAP-LAYERS.md.

default_layer.description: layer_id shown on first load. MUST name a layer in this document that requires no credential, so a fresh checkout renders something.

overlays.description: Layers drawn on top of the active basemap, e.g. street labels over satellite imagery. Same shape as a basemap layer.

label.description: Human-readable name for the layer switcher, e.g. 'Satellite'.

kind.description: The familiar map-app category. A viewer MAY group its switcher by this.

protocol.description: Tile addressing scheme. 'xyz' is the slippy-map convention with row 0 at the north. 'tms' flips the Y axis. Stated explicitly because getting it wrong silently mirrors the map vertically.

url_template.description: Tile URL with {z}, {x}, {y} placeholders, and optionally {s} for a subdomain and {key} for a credential injected at runtime. MUST NOT contain a literal credential.

subdomains.description: Values substituted for {s}, to spread requests across hostnames.

requires_credential.description: True when {key} must be supplied. The viewer reads it from its own runtime configuration or environment, never from this document.

credential_hint.description: Name of the environment variable or config field the viewer should read, e.g. 'VITE_BASEMAP_KEY_MAPTILER'. A hint, never a value.

attribution_text.description: Credit line the viewer MUST display whenever this layer is visible. Every major provider requires one; several require their logo as well.

license.description: SPDX identifier or short name, e.g. 'ODbL-1.0', 'public-domain', 'proprietary'.

usage_policy.description: Plain-language statement of what this layer may be used for, so a reviewer does not have to chase the terms. Record volume limits and commercial restrictions here.

commercial_use.description: Whether this layer may be used commercially. A viewer SHOULD warn when a non-permitted layer is selected.
